concept.name: Harami cross
concept.definition: A two-candlestick pattern in which a large real body is followed by a doji contained entirely within that body, forming a harami whose second candle is a doji. Technical analysts regard it as a more potent reversal warning than a plain harami because the doji shows the trend's momentum has stalled into outright indecision; it is bullish after declines and bearish after advances.
concept.intuition: A big confident candle is followed by a session that goes absolutely nowhere and hides inside the prior body, suggesting the driving force behind the trend has abruptly evaporated.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 has a large body; candle 2 is a doji (open approximately equal to close) whose body lies inside body 1. Bullish harami cross: large black body then doji after a downtrend. Bearish harami cross: large white body then doji after an uptrend. Confirmation comes from the next candle's direction.
concept.failure_modes: Doji are common, so harami crosses appear often in directionless markets where they carry no reversal information. Even after trends, many instances resolve as continuation once the indecision breaks the prior way.
concept.misconceptions: It is not the same as a doji star (morning/evening doji star): there the doji gaps away from the first body, while here it sits inside it. The second candle must be a true near-zero-body doji, not merely a small candle.
concept.example: After a decline, a stock prints a long black candle (30.00 to 27.00), then a doji opening at 28.10 and closing at 28.12, inside the prior body. The bullish harami cross warns of a possible bottom, pending an up close the next session.
